title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 7-10): Grothendieck is building a combinatorial 'magma' (axioms Mag 1-4) attached to a totally (or at least partially) ordered set L. It serves as a discrete model of a 1-dimensional cell structure, a 'line' with 0-cells and 1-cells. M = M_0 ⊔ M_1, where M_0 = L (points) and M_1 consists of closed intervals I_{a,b}. Each cell X has a support |X| ⊂ L and a boundary δX (for I_{a,b}, δ = {a,b}). On the previous page he enlarges M to M̂ by adjoining formal 'half-infinite' 1-cells (rays): I_{<a} for a not minimal and I_{>a} for a not maximal. These have boundary {a}, support L_{≤a} and interior L_{<a} (dually for I_{>a}). The purpose is a formalism for limits of (generalized) polygons in which δΦ = δΦ' can hold.

On this page he extends the incidence/inclusion relation ∘≪ (a non-strict 'is contained in / is a subcell of' relation; the margin note suggests that on M it amounts to inclusion of supports, X ∘≪ Y ⇔ |X| ⊂ |Y|) to the new elements:
- I_{<a} ∘≪ I_{<b} ⇔ a ≤ b.
- X ∘≪ I_{<a} ⇔ X ≤ a for X ∈ M, i.e. all of X lies weakly left of a.
- Dually for the rays I_{>a}.
- The other relations are imposed 'naturally' in the same way.

He then records two non-relations.
(a) There is never I_{<a} ∘≪ X with X ∈ M, even when L has a least element ω_0. In that case I_{ω_0,a} ∘≪ I_{<a} holds but not the converse, although |I_{ω_0,a}| = |I_{<a}| = L_{≤a}. Since ∘≪ is antisymmetric, having both would force I_{<a} = I_{ω_0,a}. That would defeat the intention that a ray is a formal, open-ended object, distinct from a finite interval with the same support ('with multiplicity'). So ∘≪ on M̂ is deliberately not determined by supports alone.
(b) There is never I_{<a} ∘≪ I_{>b}, nor the converse.

Finally he begins defining an order ≤ on M̂ extending that on M, by X ≤ Y ⇔ δX ≤ δY (every boundary point of X ≤ every boundary point of Y). He crosses this out and completes it on the next page, with extra clauses for rays and the relation X|·|Y ⇔ {X,Y} ∈ Dra_{1/2}(M̂,≤). He then checks the magma axioms.
errors: No genuine mathematical error is visible. One point needs care: ∘≪ is used non-strictly (I_{<a} ∘≪ I_{<a} holds for a = b), so the antisymmetry argument in (a) is what forbids I_{<a} ∘≪ I_{ω_0,a}. The page's remark '|I_{ω_0,a}| = |I_{<a}|' shows explicitly that the margin characterization 'X ∘≪ Y ⇔ |X| ⊂ |Y|' is valid only on M, not on M̂. This is consistent with Grothendieck's own comment.
The crossed-out definition X ≤ Y ⇔ δX ≤ δY would be inadequate on M̂ as it stands, since it would allow I_{>a} ≤ I_{<b}. Grothendieck corrects this on the next page with clause 2°.

ideas.what: Combinatorial 1-dimensional cell structure on an ordered set: points and intervals with boundary δ, support |·| and incidence ∘≪, axiomatized as a 'magma' (Mag 1-4)
ideas.modern_name: cell poset / face poset of a 1-dimensional CW or regular cell complex; combinatorial model of a stratified line
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (combinatorial topology; e.g. face posets of regular CW complexes)
ideas.where_published: unpublished 1986 notes (Ch. IX 'Ateliers'); related in spirit to the 'topologie modérée' programme in the Esquisse d'un programme

ideas.what: Adjoining formal half-infinite cells (rays) I_{<a}, I_{>a} with one-point boundary, kept distinct from a finite interval with the same support even when L has a minimum
ideas.modern_name: formal end-cells / compactification by open ends; distinction between closed segment and ray in a stratified line (cf. adding 'ends' to a cell complex)

ideas.what: Order on cells via boundaries: X ≤ Y ⇔ δX ≤ δY, adjusted for rays; the 'comparability' relation Dra_{1/2}
ideas.modern_name: interval order / order on cells of a linearly ordered complex

missed.claim: Part of an unpublished axiomatics ('magmas', axioms Mag 1-4, 'ateliers', Dra_{1/2}) for combinatorial cell structures meant to handle limits of generalized polygons. In it, incidence is deliberately not determined by supports. The system does not appear in Grothendieck's published texts.
missed.quote: En fait, I_{ω0,a} doit être vu comme ... avec multiplicité ... ceci malgré que |I_{ω0,a}| = |I_{<a}|
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of mainly historical interest: it documents Grothendieck's 1986 attempt at a combinatorial foundation for tame or stratified 1-dimensional geometry. Mathematically, this page itself is routine.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but elementary extension of an incidence relation and an order to formally adjoined ray cells. The broader 'ateliers/magmas' framework is unpublished, but nothing on this page would surprise a specialist.
transcription_corrections: Left margin likely reads 'On a X ∘≪ Y ⇔ |X| ⊂ |Y| pour X,Y ∈ M' (inclusion of supports) rather than '|X|<|Y|'.
Line 3 '$J(\ldots X\in M)$' is probably '(et pour X ∈ M)' or similar.
'les relations multiplicatives' is uncertain; it may be 'les relations implicites' ('naturelles imposées successivement').
Bottom-left margin reads approximately 'Mag 2 OK sur M̂' rather than 'M ≠ M̂ ou M̂'.
'Par exemple, quand on n'a pas' may be 'Par exemple, quoiqu'on n'a pas I_{<a} ∘≪ I_{ω0,a}, on a ... I_{ω0,a} ∘≪ I_{<a}'.
